name: Tata Steel Ltd
title: Tata Steel Ltd - 500470 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Tata Steel FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 35% YoY to Rs 34,848 crore; FY27 cost savings target Rs 7,100 crore and capex step-up to ~Rs 20,000 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 63,270 crore and EBITDA Rs 9,953 crore (16% margin), helped by higher India realisations, volumes and cost savings. India EBITDA grew 17% YoY to Rs 34,272 crore at a 24% margin, and UK plus Netherlands EBITDA turned positive for the full year. Management guided Q1 FY27 realisations up about Rs 6,000/t in India, £80/t in UK and €80/t in Netherlands. The main overhang is the Netherlands coke and gas plant (CGP) closure, which has led auditors to flag a material uncertainty on TSN's going concern, plus a delayed UK EAF grid connection.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 9,439 crore on revenue of Rs 38,448 crore

financial_highlights.change: Operating cash flow before capex and dividend ~Rs 29,254 crore vs ~Rs 17,700 crore

financial_highlights.value: Rs 10,868 crore (India ~Rs 3,927 crore, UK ~Rs 1,958 crore, Netherlands ~Rs 4,983 crore)

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: EBITDA Rs 34,272 crore in FY26 (+17% YoY) at 24% margin, in line with 10-year average; crude steel output ~23 Mt (+8% YoY), with Kalinganagar phase 2 ramp complete. NINL Q4 EBITDA Rs 402 crore (+15% QoQ, ~27% margin).

segments.name: UK (TSUK)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA -£48 million, improved £15 million QoQ; FY26 EBITDA -£217 million, narrowed £168 million YoY. Annual deliveries ~2.2 Mt; losses around £98/t cited.

segments.name: Netherlands (TSN)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA €58 million (€34/t), held back by lower realisations; FY26 EBITDA €267 million, almost tripled YoY. Liquid steel ~6.7 Mt and deliveries ~6.1 Mt; DSP plant shut after emission exceedances.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 realisations expected ~Rs 6,000/t higher than Q4 in India, of which ~30% in Q1 and ~70% in Q2 for auto contracts; ~£80/t higher in UK and ~€80/t higher in Netherlands.
Q1 FY27 coal cost up ~$15/t in India and ~$10/t in Netherlands; iron ore up ~$5/t in Netherlands. Management expects India and UK margin expansion and Netherlands margin compression.
FY27 cost transformation savings target ~Rs 7,100 crore vs FY26.
FY27 consolidated capex ~Rs 20,000 crore (from ~Rs 14,000 crore in FY26), over 60% in India.
FY27 volume at least 2 Mt higher than FY26, mostly India, driven by Kalinganagar ramp-up.
UK targeted to turn EBITDA positive during FY27; UK safeguard revision from 1 July 2026 (quota cut ~60%, tariff 25% to 50%) expected to lift prices.
NINL merger with Tata Steel to complete in FY27; NINL expansion FID expected July-September 2026, target start 2029-30.
Dividend of Rs 4 per share proposed.
capex_capacity: Kalinganagar 5 MTPA ramp-up complete; Ludhiana 0.75 MTPA scrap-based EAF commissioned and ramping (about 0.5 Mt in FY27 volumes).
NINL 5 MTPA expansion: FEL3 advanced, FID expected in July-September 2026, target 2029-30; site planned as a 10 Mt site.
India capex projects include HRPGL at Tarapur (0.8 MTPA), tinplate expansion (0.3-0.4 MTPA), Jamshedpur coke oven projects, tubes and wires, and mining projects.
UK ~3 MTPA scrap-based EAF: demolition complete; National Grid connectivity delayed, with the delay now estimated at 6-8 months or more, down from an initial 18 months to 12 months.
Netherlands: DSP plant suspended after emission exceedances, restart targeted later in May pending approvals; CGP closure timeline still under discussion with regulators.
Maharashtra greenfield site: land identified, update expected in about three months; potential 6-10 Mt.
demand_pricing: India demand outlook: management previously expected 8-10% steel demand growth but would recalibrate if GDP growth slows; auto strong, construction slowed, MSME stress noted.
Q1 FY27 price trend: prices rose in March-April-May; long products softening from secondary producers, flats firm on higher China prices (+$20-25/t in 3-4 weeks) and better export options.

Retail/branded: Tata Tiscon retail sales above 200,000 t/month (up from 100,000-120,000 t/month); Tata Steelium cold-rolled volumes ~28% YoY; Aashiyana online platform GMV ~Rs 5,000 crore, sold at Tata Steel margins.
UK safeguard: slabs excluded from quotas; UK prices had been ~£100/t below Europe and have now caught up to slightly above.
India slab transfers to UK to rise to ~1.8 Mt from ~1.2 Mt; system EBITDA ~Rs 12,000/t on slabs (Rs 7,000-8,000/t market basis plus UK share).

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost impact of closing the Netherlands coke and gas plants and buying coke?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a cost penalty from losing coke oven gas and adding freight, partly offset by lower CO2; net impact depends on timing, with coke sourced from India or elsewhere. No quantified figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did auditors flag material uncertainty on TSN going concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cause is a post-balance-sheet letter from environmental agencies on intent to revoke permits without dates or pathway; closure must be planned and safe, and CGP shutdown is expected to take time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UK EAF commissioning delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay of 6-8 months or more after plant build; initial estimate of 18 months has come down to about 12 months, with efforts to reduce further and trials planned with one line connection.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and cost guidance for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: India ~Rs 6,000/t higher QoQ, largely from prices up to May; auto contracts partly in Q1 (30%) and Q2 (70%). Other West Asia-related cost impacts not quantified yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why not faster brownfield expansion in India versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited optionality to reach 45-50 Mt on existing sites, a new approach of announcing projects only after FEL3 and approvals, and a shift of value pools to downstream amid rising iron ore and coal costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TMILL stake increase about?
qa_highlights.answer: TMILL stake rises from 51% to 74% with NYK holding the balance; TMILL has ~55 rakes and about 80% of revenue from ground and rail logistics. Slurry pipeline and waterways expansion planned.

risks_watch: Netherlands CGP closure timeline, permit revocation risk and cost penalty from buying coke; TSN going concern material uncertainty.
UK EAF power connection delay (6-8+ months) and whether UK turns EBITDA positive in FY27 given Middle East energy costs.
West Asia impact on energy, freight and inputs (propane shortage hit galvanising, tinplate and colour lines); costs not yet quantified for Q1 FY27.
Long product softness from secondary producers and possible demand slowdown from weaker GDP outlook and construction slowdown.
NINL FID (July-September 2026) and Maharashtra site update in ~3 months; mass claim defence in the Netherlands is in progress.
Iron ore cost increases and post-2030 captive lease bidding; ~$1 billion offshore ECB exposure is hedged.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India growth, cost savings and pricing, with a clear upbeat tone on Q1 realisations. Noticeably cautious and at times evasive on the Netherlands CGP closure, the timing of the NINL and Maharashtra expansions, and the Q1 West Asia cost impact, which management declined to quantify.
key_quotes: Tata Steel delivered a strong performance in FY2026, with improved margins expanding across operating geographies despite subdued pricing and challenges during the year.

We have also enhanced our working capital efficiency and released around Rs 6,000 crores of cash during the year especially in India and Netherlands through very focused management of working capital.
So, we expect them to take care of themselves.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 India volumes at least 2 Mt above FY26 (mostly from Kalinganagar ramp-up, now complete) plus Q1 FY27 realisation gains of ~Rs 6,000/t in India, £80/t in UK and €80/t in Netherlands; capex raised to ~Rs 20,000 crore for FY27, but no quantified revenue growth % was given and the UK EAF is delayed.
